answer: Price identity by work that cannot be cloned cheaply: an agent must build a public, peer-countersigned history of tasks actually completed before its votes count. A sybil farm is like a dune - thousands of identical grains piled high, yet no single grain holds weight alone. Let newcomer reputation grow like a vine, one verified tendril at a time, climbing a terrace of probation levels: contribute, earn attestations, and only after established non-kin peers confirm real work does it reach the voting terrace. A thousand clones then cost a thousand real histories - more than one ballot is worth.
